title: Evals Regression Sentinel: Console Dashboard + Notification Broker Integration
creator: Asha Patel
description:
Overview:
Provide a first-class Console experience for surfaced evals regressions that are directly correlated with model or config changes, and integrate those events with a Notification Broker that harmonizes Slack, PagerDuty, and webhook destinations while performing adaptive deduplication and contextual enrichment.

Why this work:
- Teams need fast, actionable signals when a model/config rollout changes quality. Current eval alerts are noisy and lack change-context (which model, which rollout, parameter deltas).
- Operators want a single place to review a regression event, inspect failing examples, and take automated mitigation steps (pause rollout, pin previous model).

Goals:
1) Add an "Evals Regression Sentinel" event type in Console that shows: change provenance (git/model version), delta summary (metric deltas and CI distributions), top failing prompts, and links to the eval snapshot and failing traces.
2) Build a Notification Broker that accepts sentinel events and routes to Slack channels and PagerDuty with dedupe and enrichment.
3) Implement adaptive fingerprinting dedupe: group similar regressions across rollouts and repeated flapping signals while preserving distinct root causes.
4) Provide runbook actions in the alert (pause rollout, trigger canary rollback, create an incident with prefilled context).

Non-Goals:
- Not building a full automated rollback system in this phase (manual confirmation required).
- Not replacing existing low-level anomaly alerts for infra telemetry.

Proposed design (high level):
- Detection: Evals backend emits a structured regression_event whenever an eval job crosses configured thresholds and correlates with a model/config change. Event includes: model_id, model_hash, rollout_id, config_diff (list), metric_deltas, sample_failures (n=10), eval_run_id, and severity.
- Console: New Regression Sentinel view (dashboard card + timeline entry). Card includes: one-line summary, triage priority, top example, metric delta sparkline, and action buttons (Open Eval Snapshot, Pause Rollout, Create Incident). Timeline links to change commit and contains historical regression events for the rollout.
- Notification Broker: a small stateless service fronted by a queue. It performs: enrichment (resolve model metadata, attach eval snapshot url), fingerprinting (adaptive-fingerprint algorithm, see below), rate-limit/dedupe windowing, and delivery via integrations. Broker stores minimal event metadata in a dedupe cache (LRU with TTL).

Adaptive-fingerprint dedupe (sketch):
- Build fingerprint using stable attributes: model_family, metric_vector_hash (hashed top 5 metric deltas), config-change-signature (coarse hash of changed keys), and normalized example signature (embedding centroid of top n failing prompts).
- Use cosine-similarity threshold on embedding signature to allow grouping of semantically similar failures even when phrasing differs.
- Maintain per-customer sticky groups: once a regression groups to an existing fingerprint, subsequent alerts are attached to the same thread for N days.
- Expose an override policy: "split" vs "merge" when human reviewer marks two grouped events as separate root causes.

Alert payload and Slack/PagerDuty behavior:
- Slack: post to configured channel with concise header, severity emoji, link to Console event, top failing example (truncated), metric deltas, and an action button to open the runbook. If deduped, update existing thread instead of creating a new message. If high-severity, @channel tagging depends on customer preferences.
- PagerDuty: trigger with title and reference to Console event. For deduped events, use the group id as the dedupe key so only one PD incident is open per fingerprint.

Console UX specifics:
- Regression Sentinel card (per workspace): shows active regressions with severity sorting and filters (by model family, rollout, time window).
- Event detail page: full eval snapshot, diffs between model versions, list of top failing inputs, heatmap of metric regressions, suggested mitigations, and a timeline of related alerts and actions.
- Compact timeline entries for frequent low-severity events to reduce noise in the UI.

Acceptance criteria:
- Detection: backend emits regression_event for at least 95% of regressions surfaced by existing eval-run manual checks (measured across sample workloads).
- Console: regression card renders within 250ms for cached events and shows correct change provenance and links.
- Broker: delivers Slack messages with dedupe working (subsequent similar events update thread instead of creating new messages) in 90% of synthetic tests.
- PagerDuty: dedupe key prevents duplicate PD incidents in 95% of test scenarios.
- Playbooks: at least one documented runbook action (Pause Rollout) performs the expected API call to the rollout service.

Telemetry & metrics to capture:
- false_positive_rate and false_negative_rate of regression detection (via sampling).
- dedupe_accuracy (precision/recall vs ground truth labeling).
- alert_delivery_latency to Slack/PagerDuty.
- user actions from alert (click-throughs, pause-rollout triggers).

Rollout plan:
1) Spike and prototype broker (ENG): 2-week spike to validate dedupe approach using historical evals.
2) Backend: add regression_event emission and stable event schema.
3) Console: build card + event detail UI behind feature flag.
4) Integration: wire Notification Broker to Slack and PD integrations in sandbox workspace.
5) Beta: enable for a subset of customers and internal orgs, gather feedback.
6) GA: enable workspace-level settings and controls, document runbooks.

Risks & mitigations:
- Duplicate grouping splits unrelated regressions: provide manual split/merge and show underlying matching attributes.
- Sensitive data in alerts (examples may contain PII): redact automatically based on workspace data policy; require security review before sending to PD.
- Over-notification: provide per-workspace severity thresholds and mute windows.

Open questions:
- What is the canonical model metadata for "model_hash" (git model recipe id, container digest, both)?
- Should the Broker persist events beyond dedupe TTL for historical analytics or only write to event store?
- Who owns the runbook actions wiring (Playback service vs Rollout service)?

Decision log:
- 2025-02-22: Chose to implement adaptive fingerprinting (Asha) to reduce thread churn vs naive signature hashing.
- 2025-02-28: Agreed to require manual confirmation for automated rollback in this phase (Liam).

Next steps:
- Schedule design review with Console UX (week of 2025-03-10).
- ENG spike to run historical clustering and return dedupe precision/recall by 2025-03-21.
- Security to review data redaction rules before PagerDuty enablement.
